title: Pharaoh's Boasting and Jesus as an Example

paragraphs.text: But as soon as Allah removed the hardship, they broke their promise. Pharaoh then called out to his people, boasting that the kingdom of Egypt and the rivers flowing beneath him belonged to him. "Do you not see?" he asked them. He asked whether he was not better than Moses, whom he called insignificant and barely able to speak clearly. He mocked Moses, asking why he had no golden bracelets and why no angels came with him. In this way Pharaoh fooled his people, and they obeyed him, because they were themselves defiantly disobedient. When they angered Allah, He punished them and drowned them all, making them a lesson and an example for later generations.

When the son of Mary was presented as an example, the Prophet's people laughed aloud. They asked whether the things they worshipped were better than he, but they only said this for the sake of argument, because they love to quarrel. Jesus was nothing more than a servant on whom Allah bestowed His favor, and Allah made him an example for the Children of Israel. If Allah willed, He could have placed angels on the earth to succeed one another instead of humans. Jesus is a sign for knowing the Hour, so there should be no doubt about it. People should follow the straight path and never let Satan turn them away, since he is a clear enemy.

When Jesus came with clear proofs, he said he had brought wisdom and would explain some of their disagreements. He told them to fear Allah and obey him, because Allah is his Lord and their Lord, and worshipping Him is the straight path. However, the groups among them disagreed and split, so woe to the wrongdoers from the punishment of a painful Day. What are they waiting for, except the Hour, which will come upon them suddenly while they do not even notice it?

hardWords.m: to come after and take the place of
